title: Boundedness from a closed graph
promptMarkdown:
Let $T:C([0,1])\to C([0,1])$ be a linear map (sup norm on both sides) with the following property: whenever $f_n\to f$ uniformly and $Tf_n\to g$ uniformly, one has $Tf=g$.

1. Prove that $T$ is bounded.
2. Let $D$ be differentiation, defined on the subspace $C^1_0=\{g\in C^1([0,1]):g(0)=0\}$ with the sup norm, mapping into $C([0,1])$. Show that $D$ has a closed graph (if $g_n\to g$ and $g_n'\to h$ uniformly then $g\in C^1_0$ and $g'=h$), yet $D$ is unbounded (unit 2). Explain precisely why this does not contradict part 1.
hintLadder: The stated property says exactly that the graph of $T$ is closed in $C([0,1])\times C([0,1])$. Which theorem applies, and are its hypotheses satisfied?
For 2: uniform convergence of derivatives together with convergence at one point lets you integrate: $g_n(x)=\int_0^x g_n'$. Pass to the limit.
The closed graph theorem has two completeness hypotheses. Is $C^1_0$ with the sup norm complete?

deterministicChecks.description: the closed graph theorem needs both spaces complete

criteria.criterion: Identifies the property as closedness of the graph.
Applies the closed graph theorem with both spaces Banach (C([0,1]) complete, Theorem 16).
Shows the graph of D is closed using uniform convergence of derivatives and integration from 0.
C¹₀ with the sup norm is not complete, so the theorem does not apply; names a Cauchy sequence in C¹₀ with non-C¹ uniform limit or cites unit 2's sequence.

checkExamples.label: hypotheses stated
checkExamples.text: C([0,1]) with the sup norm is a Banach space, the graph of T is closed by hypothesis, so the closed graph theorem gives boundedness.

checkExamples.label: hypothesis omitted
checkExamples.text: The graph is closed, so by the closed graph theorem T is bounded.
